newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Death threats against Colombian soccer chiefs.
newsitem.headline: Death threats against Colombian soccer chiefs.

text.p: The coach of Colombia's national soccer squad received death threats after the team's crushing 4-1 defeat by Chile last weekend, local media reported on Friday.

Coach Hernan Dario Gomez, nicknamed the "Nightstick" for his often abrasive treatment of players and the press, said he began getting anonymous calls on his return to Colombia on Monday, adding that National Soccer Federation chairman Alvaro Fina was also threatened.

"The threats started coming after the 4-1 loss to Chile," Gomez said during a televised news conference in the coastal city of Barranquilla, where the team is in training for its upcoming match against Ecuador.

"Some of the (media) reports that have appeared in recent days have put at risk my security and that of the squad," he added, taking a swipe at recent press criticism of his management and the team's performance.

After an early unbeaten run in its World Cup qualifying campaign, Colombia has slumped to four defeats in five games. It is still hanging onto third place, behind Paraguay and Argentina, in the battle for four South American places in France next year.
Colombia needs to win at least three of its final four matches to make the World Cup.

The threats recalled the memory of Andres Escobar, the Colombian defender shot to death outside a Medellin restaurant after accidentally knocking the ball into his own goal during Colombia's 1994 World Cup loss to the United States.
